governance.note: neiso-56 = the neiso-55 keeper recipe (byte-identical run_config, CLI flags, winter fuel-security stack, reliability drag, temp_dependent_derate) with ONE structural addition: energy_reserve_coopt=True — the ISO-NE system-wide energy+reserve co-optimization with the published 3-level nested RCPF demand curves (reserve_config._neiso_design / NEISO_RCPF_PRODUCTS: total-30-min 1,800 MW @ $1,000, total-10-min 1,200 MW @ $1,500, 10-min-spin 600 MW @ $50; ISO-NE Market Rule 1 Section III.2.7A reserve constraint penalty factors), storage reserve-eligible. The requirements and penalties are published market-design constants, NOT tuned to the backcast (rule 13: they regenerate forward unchanged and respond to changed conditions). PROBE registered per rule 14; NOT promoted. Result recorded honestly: the mechanism is decisively DORMANT on 2023-2025 — the reserve balance dual is $0.00 in all 26,280 hours (both P1 and P2), the ample NEISO fleet clears the nested requirements out of idle headroom at zero opportunity cost (the caiso-59/MISO inert-family signature); C3c tail unchanged at 0h >$300 every year; C5b storage discharge byte-similar to the keeper (0.579/0.521/0.827 vs 0.578/0.521/0.828 TWh); fuel mix byte-comparable (no class moves >0.05 TWh). This closes the C5b ledger's named closure-path inventory: both the winter fuel-security build (G-24, exhausted 2026-07-07) and in-LP reserve co-optimization are now proven dormant on these backcast years. No lever is fitted to a price residual and no input is pinned to actuals.

exceptions.metric: hours LMP > $300/MWh (C3c scarcity tail, DA-expressible / NEISO $300 threshold)
exceptions.magnitude: model 0h vs DA actual 5h (RT 15h); system max ~$249
exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (NEISO winter scarcity-price formation; winter fuel-security build adopted, DORMANT on this backcast; temp_dependent_derate also dormant on the tail); energy_reserve_coopt (neiso-56) also dormant on the tail
exceptions.reason: The energy-only LP caps the cold-hour price at dual-fuel oil-parity (~$258/MWh). The adopted winter fuel-inventory / seasonal-reliability build (neiso_gas_coldsnap_derate + neiso_winter_fuel_inventory + neiso_winter_fuel_mustrun) is DORMANT on 2023-2025: the derate removes too little capacity on too few hours to make the ample NEISO winter fleet reserve-short, so Component A's oil budget never binds and the >$300 tail does not form (model 0h, unchanged vs the zero-forcing ablation twin). temp_dependent_derate does NOT change this: its CC/CT reshape is capacity-neutral over summer and its additive COAL/ST_GAS hot-hour derate does not touch the winter cold-hour hours where NEISO's tail actually forms - hoursGt300 is 0h in every year with and without the derate. This is a winter capacity-adequacy / scarcity-price-formation gap, NOT closable by these mechanisms here and NEVER by an offer adder tuned to the tail. neiso-56 adds the in-LP ISO-NE RCPF reserve co-optimization on this exact recipe: the reserve balance dual is $0.00 in every hour of all three years — no cold-snap hour goes reserve-short at the published 1,800/1,200/600 MW requirements — so the RCPF never stacks into the LMP and the >$300 tail still does not form.

exceptions.magnitude: model 0.83 vs actual 2.08 TWh (-60.2%; unchanged vs the neiso-55 keeper)
exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (downstream of the price_tail / winter-scarcity item)
exceptions.reason: PS arbitrage throughput tracks the intraday price spread. The residual under-cycle is winter-concentrated: the LP's cold-month spread stays compressed at the dual-fuel oil-parity cap, and the real Northfield fleet additionally cycles near-daily for reserves/regulation the energy-only LP does not remunerate. Per the neiso-ps-undercycling diagnosis the PS number may only move DOWNSTREAM of price structure, never via a storage knob. temp_dependent_derate slightly DEEPENS the gap (-56.3% -> -60.2%): the capacity-neutral summer reshape trims a little of the shoulder-season spread the PS fleet was arbitraging, without adding winter spread. Closes only with the winter fuel-inventory build and/or in-LP reserve co-optimization value reaching storage; never via a storage knob. neiso-56 tested the ledger's named closure path — in-LP reserve co-optimization value reaching storage (storage reserve-eligible in the co-opt) — and it is DORMANT: reserves clear free from idle thermal headroom, no reserve value reaches the pumped-storage fleet, and discharge is byte-similar to the keeper (0.827 vs 0.828 TWh in 2025).

exceptions.metric: C2 gas family grid-delivered TWh (preliminary 2025 vintage)
exceptions.magnitude: +2.6% vs corrected EIA-930 grid gas (commercial band)
exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (EIA-930 gas-vs-OTHER fold-in + preliminary-vintage incompleteness)
exceptions.reason: 2025 is a preliminary EIA-923 vintage - per-class actuals are incomplete (13/30 prior CC_REGULAR plants missing, 57% reporting). The scorer falls back to the EIA-930 grid gas cell, which includes geothermal+biomass; the correction formula under-corrects because the preliminary vintage's per-class cells are incomplete. Same categorization issue as the complete-vintage years, where the per-class C1 gate PASSES under the load-scaled band. NOT closable by adjusting model dispatch. Unchanged by temp_dependent_derate.

exceptions.metric: C1 coal + steam-gas winter-energy under-run (within the C1 band, non-gating; documentation)
exceptions.magnitude: COAL_BIT model ~0.06/0.11/0.23 vs actual 0.18/0.24/0.27 TWh (2023/24/25); ST_GAS similar
exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (structural; same winter fuel-security family as price_tail and storage)
exceptions.reason: The energy-only LP runs coal/steam only at the temperature-floor commitment plus the hours delivered gas is dear enough; the real units ran more on winter fuel-security / local-reliability commitments. Closable only via the documented winter fuel-inventory / seasonal-reliability build, never by cranking the floor slope/cap or an offer adder. Within the C1 band, non-gating. Unchanged by temp_dependent_derate.
